```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", echo = FALSE, message = FALSE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
```

`read_bam` reads a file in one of two ways. By default htslib opens it with its own file
access, which for an `http://` URL is htslib's libcurl backend. After
`SET duckhts_file_system = 'duckdb'` the same htslib decoder reads through the DuckDB file
system of the connection, which for an `http://` URL is the httpfs extension
(`src/duckdb_fs_hfile.c`). This report compares the two routes on the same file, the same
server and the same queries: record counts, wall time, peak memory, and the HTTP requests
each route sends.

## What is held equal

Both routes run the same BAM decoder with the same htslib tuning. DuckHTS chooses that
tuning from the path the user gave, not from the route (`src/include/hts_io_tuning.h`):

```{r tuning}
source("benchmarks/duckdb_file_system_run.R")
knitr::kable(file_system_tuning, col.names = c("Scan", "hFILE block (MiB)", "BGZF block cache (MiB)"))
```

The hFILE block is the size of each read htslib asks its file backend for.
`SET duckhts_remote_block_size` replaces it; every section but the one that varies it
leaves that setting at 0, the automatic size in the table. The BGZF cache size has no
setting. htslib's libcurl
backend has further controls that this benchmark leaves at their defaults: the retry and
low-speed environment variables (`HTS_RETRY_MAX`, `HTS_RETRY_DELAY`, `HTS_RETRY_MAX_DELAY`,
`HTS_LOW_SPEED_LIMIT`, `HTS_LOW_SPEED_TIME`) and its rule to read on, without a new
request, across a forward seek shorter than 1 MB (`MIN_SEEK_FORWARD` in
`third_party/htslib/hfile_libcurl.c`). httpfs runs with its default settings, except in
the section that varies them.

Both routes load httpfs before the timed query, so neither pays for loading it.

## Inputs and method

```{r run, include=FALSE}
artifact_ids <- c("1x" = "insert_size_hg00403_chr20_bam",
                  "2x" = "insert_size_hg00403_chr20_bam_2x",
                  "4x" = "insert_size_hg00403_chr20_bam_4x")
bams <- vapply(artifact_ids, duckhtsbench::duckhts_bench_artifact_path, "")
extension <- "build/release/duckhts.duckdb_extension"
result <- file_system_benchmark(extension, bams, region_repetitions = params$region_reps,
                                scan_repetitions = params$scan_reps)
file_system_check(result)
runs <- result$runs
summary <- file_system_summary(runs)
utils::write.csv(runs[names(runs) != "digest"],
                 "benchmarks/benchmark_duckdb_file_system_runs.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r identity}
status <- system2("git", c("status", "--porcelain", "--", "src", "duckdb_capi", "CMakeLists.txt"),
                  stdout = TRUE)
cpu <- unique(sub("^model name\\s*:\\s*", "", grep("^model name", readLines("/proc/cpuinfo"), value = TRUE)))
identity <- data.frame(
  item = c("source revision", "source tree", "extension md5", "htslib", "R", "DuckDB R package",
           "httpfs", "CPU", "logical CPUs", "DuckDB memory limit", "DuckDB temp directory limit",
           "server", "repetitions"),
  value = c(system2("git", c("rev-parse", "HEAD"), stdout = TRUE),
            if (length(status)) "modified" else "clean",
            unname(tools::md5sum(extension)),
            readLines("third_party/htslib/VERSION", n = 1),
            R.version.string,
            sprintf("%s (DuckDB %s)", packageVersion("duckdb"), paste(unique(runs$duckdb_version), collapse = ", ")),
            sprintf("%s, default settings except where a section varies them",
                    paste(unique(stats::na.omit(runs$httpfs_version)), collapse = ", ")),
            cpu[[1L]], as.character(parallel::detectCores()), "2 GiB", "0 B (no spill allowed)",
            "scripts/benchmark_range_server.py on 127.0.0.1, one thread per connection",
            sprintf("%d per region workload, %d per scan workload; one fresh R process each, routes alternated",
                    params$region_reps, params$scan_reps))
)
knitr::kable(identity)
```

The inputs are the chromosome 20 alignments of 1000 Genomes sample HG00403 and their
doubled and quadrupled copies, staged by `r/duckhtsbench`. `samtools view -c` gives the
record count that every measurement must return:

```{r inputs}
inputs <- data.frame(
  scale = names(bams), artifact = unname(artifact_ids),
  bytes = file.size(bams), index_bytes = file.size(paste0(bams, ".bai"))
)
oracle <- result$oracle
oracle$region[is.na(oracle$region)] <- "whole file"
knitr::kable(inputs, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
knitr::kable(oracle[c("scale", "region", "records")], format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
             col.names = c("Scale", "Region", "Records (samtools)"))
```

Each query is
`SELECT count(*), sum(hash(QNAME, FLAG, POS, CIGAR)) FROM read_bam(url [, region := ...])`.
It decodes four fields of every record and returns one row. A run passes only when its
count equals the samtools count, its hash equals the hash of every other run on that input,
DuckDB spilled nothing, and its peak resident memory stayed under the ceiling set before
measuring.

The server adds a fixed delay before it answers each request: 0 ms, and 20 ms to stand
for a network round trip. It does not limit bandwidth. Client and server share one host,
so these timings show what each route costs per request and per byte on a loopback
connection; they are not timings for an object store or a wide-area network.

## Memory budget

The idle process (extension and httpfs loaded, nothing read) peaks at
`r sprintf("%.0f", max(result$idle$peak_rss_mib))` MiB. The ceiling for a run is that
overhead plus three times the I/O state of its open handles: one hFILE block, one BGZF
block cache and one `r file_system_read_ahead_mib` MiB read-ahead buffer per handle. A
region query and a single-thread scan hold one handle; a scan on four threads holds four.
A run with a block size set budgets that size for the hFILE block. The query itself keeps
no rows: it aggregates as it reads.

## Region queries

One thread, the 1× file, regions that start at chr20:10,000,000.

```{r regions}
show <- function(rows) {
  table <- summary[rows, ]
  data.frame(
    region = ifelse(is.na(table$region), "whole file", table$region),
    scale = table$scale, `delay ms` = table$latency_ms, threads = table$threads,
    route = table$route, records = table$records,
    `median s` = table$median_seconds,
    `range s` = sprintf("%.3f-%.3f", table$min_seconds, table$max_seconds),
    `peak RSS MiB` = table$max_peak_rss_mib, `ceiling MiB` = table$rss_ceiling_mib,
    GETs = table$get_requests, `open-ended` = table$open_ended_ranges,
    `closed ranges` = table$closed_ranges, `largest range MiB` = table$max_closed_range_mib,
    `body MiB written` = table$body_mib_written, check.names = FALSE
  )
}
knitr::kable(show(summary$workload == "region"), digits = 3, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

"Open-ended" counts `Range: bytes=N-` requests, which ask for everything from an offset
to the end of the file. "Body MiB written" is what the server handed to the socket. For an
open-ended range that the client abandons, it includes bytes the client never read, so on
the htslib route it is an upper bound on the bytes received.

## Whole-file scans

Served with no added delay at 1×, 2× and 4×, on one and four DuckDB threads. The last
two rows read the 1× file from the local disk through each route.

```{r scans}
knitr::kable(show(summary$workload == "scan"), digits = 3, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## httpfs settings

The 100 kb and 10 Mb regions of the 1× file on one thread, on the DuckDB route under
httpfs settings that each differ from the defaults in one respect, `r params$scan_reps`
runs each. The `htslib` rows are the htslib route at its defaults, for reference.

```{r settings}
settings_result <- file_system_settings_benchmark(extension, bams[["1x"]], repetitions = params$scan_reps)
settings_runs <- settings_result$runs
settings_summary <- file_system_settings_summary(settings_runs)
utils::write.csv(settings_runs[names(settings_runs) != "digest"],
                 "benchmarks/benchmark_duckdb_file_system_settings_runs.csv", row.names = FALSE)
statements <- vapply(c(list(htslib = character()), file_system_httpfs_settings),
                     function(statement) paste(sub("^SET ", "", statement), collapse = "; "), "")
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  region = settings_summary$region, `delay ms` = settings_summary$latency_ms,
  setting = settings_summary$setting, `SET` = unname(statements[settings_summary$setting]),
  `median s` = settings_summary$median_seconds,
  `range s` = sprintf("%.3f-%.3f", settings_summary$min_seconds, settings_summary$max_seconds),
  `peak RSS MiB` = settings_summary$max_peak_rss_mib, GETs = settings_summary$get_requests,
  `largest range MiB` = settings_summary$max_closed_range_mib,
  `body MiB written` = settings_summary$body_mib_written, check.names = FALSE
), digits = 3, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## Block size

The same two regions on one thread, on both routes, with `duckhts_remote_block_size` at
each value below, `r params$scan_reps` runs each. `auto` is 0, which for a region query
is 1 MiB. The environment variable `DUCKHTS_BENCH_EXTRA_R_LIBS` names further R libraries
that each hold another version of the duckdb package; the same extension binary is
loaded into each.

```{r block-size}
extra_libraries <- strsplit(Sys.getenv("DUCKHTS_BENCH_EXTRA_R_LIBS"), .Platform$path.sep, fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
block_result <- file_system_block_size_benchmark(
  extension, bams[["1x"]], r_libraries = c(list(NULL), as.list(extra_libraries)),
  repetitions = params$scan_reps
)
block_runs <- block_result$runs
block_summary <- file_system_block_size_summary(block_runs)
utils::write.csv(block_runs[names(block_runs) != "digest"],
                 "benchmarks/benchmark_duckdb_file_system_block_size_runs.csv", row.names = FALSE)
block_label <- function(bytes) ifelse(bytes == 0, "auto", sprintf("%g MiB", bytes / 2^20))
# One row per value of `by`, one column per block size, holding `value`.
block_pivot <- function(value, by) {
  wide <- stats::reshape(block_summary[c(by, "block_size", value)], idvar = by,
                         timevar = "block_size", direction = "wide")
  sizes <- as.numeric(sub(paste0("^", value, "\\."), "", names(wide)[-seq_along(by)]))
  names(wide) <- c(by, block_label(sizes))
  rownames(wide) <- NULL
  wide
}
by <- c("duckdb_version", "region", "latency_ms", "route")
header <- c("DuckDB", "region", "delay ms", "route")
engines <- unique(block_runs[c("duckdb_version", "httpfs_version")])
knitr::kable(engines, row.names = FALSE, col.names = c("DuckDB", "httpfs"))
```

Median seconds:

```{r block-size-seconds}
seconds_wide <- block_pivot("median_seconds", by)
knitr::kable(seconds_wide, digits = 3, col.names = c(header, names(seconds_wide)[-(1:4)]))
```

GET requests (median):

```{r block-size-gets}
gets_wide <- block_pivot("get_requests", by)
knitr::kable(gets_wide, col.names = c(header, names(gets_wide)[-(1:4)]))
```

Body MiB the server wrote (median):

```{r block-size-bytes}
bytes_wide <- block_pivot("body_mib_written", by)
knitr::kable(bytes_wide, digits = 1, col.names = c(header, names(bytes_wide)[-(1:4)]))
```

Peak resident memory across these runs was at most
`r sprintf("%.0f", max(block_runs$peak_rss_mib))` MiB, at a block size of
`r block_label(block_runs$block_size[which.max(block_runs$peak_rss_mib)])`.

## Scaling

Time exponent for each doubling of the input, `log2(t(2n) / t(n))`, from the median
times above. For region queries the input is the region width from 2.5 Mb to 5 Mb to
10 Mb; for scans it is the file from 1× to 2× to 4×.

```{r scaling}
exponent <- function(rows, order_by) {
  table <- summary[rows, ]
  groups <- split(table, list(table$route, table$latency_ms, table$threads), drop = TRUE)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(groups, function(group) {
    group <- group[order(order_by(group)), ]
    stopifnot(nrow(group) == 3L, all(diff(group$records) > 0))
    data.frame(route = group$route[[1L]], `delay ms` = group$latency_ms[[1L]],
               threads = group$threads[[1L]],
               `records 1x` = group$records[[1L]],
               `seconds 1x` = group$median_seconds[[1L]],
               `exponent 1x to 2x` = log2(group$median_seconds[[2L]] / group$median_seconds[[1L]]),
               `exponent 2x to 4x` = log2(group$median_seconds[[3L]] / group$median_seconds[[2L]]),
               `record ratio 1x to 2x` = group$records[[2L]] / group$records[[1L]],
               `record ratio 2x to 4x` = group$records[[3L]] / group$records[[2L]],
               check.names = FALSE)
  }))
}
wide <- summary$workload == "region" & !grepl("-10100000$", summary$region)
region_scaling <- exponent(wide, function(group) group$records)
scan_scaling <- exponent(summary$workload == "scan" & !is.na(summary$latency_ms),
                         function(group) group$records)
longest_1x <- max(c(region_scaling$`seconds 1x`, scan_scaling$`seconds 1x`[scan_scaling$threads == 1L]))
```

Region width, 1× is the 2.5 Mb region:

```{r scaling-region}
knitr::kable(region_scaling, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

File size:

```{r scaling-scan}
knitr::kable(scan_scaling, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

`STYLE.md` asks for a 1× run of at least 5 s on one thread before a timing verdict. The
longest single-thread 1× run here takes `r sprintf("%.2f", longest_1x)` s, so these
exponents describe the measured runs and carry no verdict, and none may be read as a
statement about larger inputs than those measured.

## What the measurements show

```{r findings, include=FALSE}
pick <- function(route, region, latency) {
  summary[summary$workload == "region" & summary$route == route &
            summary$region == region & summary$latency_ms == latency, ]
}
widest <- "chr20:10000000-20000000"
htslib_0 <- pick("htslib", widest, 0)
duckdb_0 <- pick("duckdb", widest, 0)
htslib_20 <- pick("htslib", widest, 20)
duckdb_20 <- pick("duckdb", widest, 20)
stopifnot(nrow(htslib_0) == 1L, nrow(duckdb_0) == 1L, nrow(htslib_20) == 1L, nrow(duckdb_20) == 1L)
added <- function(pair_20, pair_0) (pair_20$median_seconds - pair_0$median_seconds) / pair_20$get_requests * 1000
setting_row <- function(setting, latency) {
  settings_summary[settings_summary$setting == setting & settings_summary$region == widest &
                     settings_summary$latency_ms == latency, ]
}
forced <- setting_row("force_download", 20)
default_20 <- setting_row("defaults", 20)
stopifnot(nrow(forced) == 1L, nrow(default_20) == 1L)
gets <- function(setting) settings_summary$get_requests[settings_summary$setting == setting]
unchanged_settings <- Filter(function(setting) identical(gets(setting), gets("defaults")),
                             setdiff(names(file_system_httpfs_settings), "defaults"))
unchanged_text <- paste0("`", unchanged_settings, "`", collapse = ", ")
setting_seconds <- function(setting, region, latency) {
  row <- settings_summary$setting == setting & settings_summary$region == region &
    settings_summary$latency_ms == latency
  stopifnot(sum(row) == 1L)
  sprintf("%.2f", settings_summary$median_seconds[row])
}
narrow <- "chr20:10000000-10100000"
# One sentence per DuckDB version on the 10 Mb region with 20 ms per request.
block_findings <- vapply(unique(block_summary$duckdb_version), function(version) {
  rows <- block_summary[block_summary$duckdb_version == version & block_summary$region == widest &
                          block_summary$latency_ms == 20, ]
  routed <- rows[rows$route == "duckdb", ]
  automatic <- routed[routed$block_size == 0, ]
  fastest <- routed[which.min(routed$median_seconds), ]
  reference <- rows[rows$route == "htslib" & rows$block_size == 0, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(automatic) == 1L, nrow(reference) == 1L)
  sprintf(paste("  - DuckDB %s: the DuckDB route took %.2f s with %.0f GETs at the automatic size and",
                "%.2f s with %.0f GETs at its fastest size, %s; the htslib route took %.2f s with",
                "%.0f GETs at the automatic size."),
          version, automatic$median_seconds, automatic$get_requests, fastest$median_seconds,
          fastest$get_requests, block_label(fastest$block_size), reference$median_seconds,
          reference$get_requests)
}, "")
```

- **Same rows.** All `r nrow(runs)` runs returned the samtools record count and one hash
  per input, on both routes.
- **Request pattern.** On the 10 Mb region the htslib route sent
  `r htslib_0$get_requests` GET requests, `r htslib_0$open_ended_ranges` of them
  open-ended; the DuckDB route sent `r duckdb_0$get_requests`, all closed ranges, the
  largest `r sprintf("%.0f", duckdb_0$max_closed_range_mib)` MiB. Across the four region
  widths the DuckDB route's count rises with the bytes read and the htslib route's count
  stays the same; in the whole-file scans both rise, the DuckDB route's far more. No
  closed range in any run exceeded `r sprintf("%.0f", max(runs$max_closed_range_bytes, na.rm = TRUE) / 2^20)` MiB.
  htslib asks its backend for at most one hFILE block at a time (`refill_buffer` in
  `third_party/htslib/hfile.c`), and every scan here, the single-thread ones included,
  runs under the 1 MiB profile: a full scan of an indexed BAM is cut into pieces
  (`src/bam_reader.c`, `is_parallel`).
- **Block size.** On the 10 Mb region with 20 ms per request:
`r paste(block_findings, collapse = "\n")`
- **httpfs settings.** `r unchanged_text` left
  the GET count of both regions equal to the defaults. `force_download` replaced the ranges
  with `r forced$get_requests` requests for the whole file: the 10 Mb region with 20 ms per
  request took `r sprintf("%.2f", forced$median_seconds)` s against
  `r sprintf("%.2f", default_20$median_seconds)` s at the defaults, at a peak of
  `r sprintf("%.0f", forced$max_peak_rss_mib)` MiB resident and
  `r sprintf("%.0f", forced$body_mib_written)` MiB sent for a `r sprintf("%.0f", file.size(bams[["1x"]]) / 2^20)` MiB file.
- **Per-request cost.** With no added delay the 10 Mb region took
  `r sprintf("%.2f", htslib_0$median_seconds)` s through htslib and
  `r sprintf("%.2f", duckdb_0$median_seconds)` s through DuckDB. With 20 ms added per
  request it took `r sprintf("%.2f", htslib_20$median_seconds)` s and
  `r sprintf("%.2f", duckdb_20$median_seconds)` s. The extra time per GET is
  `r sprintf("%.0f", added(htslib_20, htslib_0))` ms on the htslib route and
  `r sprintf("%.0f", added(duckdb_20, duckdb_0))` ms on the DuckDB route.
- **Connection settings.** With the same GET count, `http_keep_alive = false` took
  `r setting_seconds("no_keep_alive", narrow, 0)` s on the 100 kb region with no added
  delay against `r setting_seconds("defaults", narrow, 0)` s at the defaults, and
  `r setting_seconds("no_keep_alive", widest, 0)` s against
  `r setting_seconds("defaults", widest, 0)` s on the 10 Mb region. With 20 ms per request
  the 10 Mb region took `r setting_seconds("no_keep_alive", widest, 20)` s against
  `r setting_seconds("defaults", widest, 20)` s. `httpfs_connection_caching = false` gave
  times within the run-to-run range of those. This report does not establish why reusing
  connections costs time against this server.
- **Memory.** In the route comparison, peak resident memory stayed between
  `r sprintf("%.0f", min(runs$peak_rss_mib))` and `r sprintf("%.0f", max(runs$peak_rss_mib))` MiB,
  under every ceiling, and no run spilled.

## Not measured

- The block size was varied for region queries on one thread only, not for whole-file
  scans or several threads. The BGZF cache size was not varied.
- httpfs settings beyond those in the table, and combinations of them. Whether the
  external file cache serves reads made through the C file API was not examined.
- The route comparison, the scans and the httpfs settings ran on the DuckDB version of the
  first table only.
- Real object stores, TLS, bandwidth limits, and connections that fail or stall.
- CRAM, SAM, and any reader other than `read_bam`.
- Writing: the DuckDB route is read-only.
